v2 CORRECTS v1's ROSTER, WHICH WAS ARITHMETICALLY WRONG WHEN PUBLISHED AND IS FOUR ROWS STALE NOW. v1's THREE FINDINGS ALL STAND as mechanisms: the class generalises past the r0-only filter (FINDING 1), it is one-directional (FINDING 2), and the surplus copy and the over-hoist are one joint event rather than two (FINDING 3). Only the numbers are superseded.

THE PUBLISHED COUNT DISAGREES WITH v1'S OWN ENUMERATION. v1 states VERBATIM: 'Per-function populations paired on the shape-B count: P (ours more copies) = 40, Q (equal, nonzero) = 24, R (both zero) = 2919, S (ours FEWER copies) = 0.' It then enumerates the roster it tells a lane to screen -- 'The corrected P roster to screen before probing any "extra address copy" residual: adstream::AdsPutBuffer, gamemain::{do_stats_display, fn_80051E1C, fn_8005351C, init_next_level_8005638C, fn_80057024}, ...' through '... sounds_evt::AudioSetupBossStreams, bosscam::TriggerCamUpdate.' THAT LIST HOLDS 41 NAMES, NOT 40. The discrepancy is in the record as accepted; it is not a later drift.

THE ROSTER AT HEAD, MEASURED FOR THIS RECORD at e5eb50945 with v1's own reproduction command `python tools/gdl/addrlo_home_general_census.py` (exit 0): `shape A (direct home) target 920 ours 891`, `shape B (copy paid) target 33 ours 72`, and `P ours MORE copies (divergence) : 37`, `Q equal, nonzero : 24`, `R both zero : 2922`, `S ours FEWER copies (inverse) : 0`. Against v1's `target 920 / ours 887` and `target 33 / ours 75`. THE ACCOUNTING CLOSES EXACTLY, which is why this is a roster correction and not a suspicion: the 37 rows printed at HEAD are v1's 41 enumerated names MINUS exactly four -- gamemain::init_next_level_8005638C, pb_error::fn_800C13CC, pb_error::fn_800C1174 and gauntworld::ResolveWorldData. 41 - 4 = 37, with no row entering. A lane screening against v1's list today is told to screen four functions that are no longer in the class, and is told the population is 40 when it was 41 and is now 37.

S = 0 IS THE NEGATIVE CONTROL AND IT HOLDS. v1's FINDING 2 -- 'S = 0 SURVIVES THE GENERALISATION, OVER 953 OPPORTUNITIES' -- reproduces verbatim at HEAD: the tool prints `--- POPULATION S (inverse) (n=0) ---` with an empty table. The one-directionality that justifies reading the class as allocator-internal is undisturbed by the roster shrinking, and v1's disposition (the class is a named one-instruction residual, WebFrank-ineligible per claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual.20260831.v1, do not probe the B half) stands unchanged.

ONE FIGURE IN v1 IS NOT RECONCILED AND IS FLAGGED AS A CANDIDATE, NOT A BUG. v1's FINDING 3 reports 'TARGET shape-B in shadow 2/33'; at HEAD the same tool prints `TARGET  shape-B in shadow: 8   not in shadow: 25`, i.e. 8/33 -- same denominator, different numerator, on the TARGET side. The target stream is the dtk-split retail image and cannot move, and `git log --oneline -- tools/gdl/addrlo_home_general_census.py` returns exactly one commit (3eb63a60b), so the tool has never been edited; the printing loop reads only the target store (`for side, store in (("TARGET", tgt), ("OURS", ours))`, counting `h["shadow"]` over `common`). Something must therefore be wrong, but this record does NOT assert which: the candidates are that v1's 2/33 was transcribed from one of the two OTHER tools its provenance names (`addrlo_dest_census.py`, `addrlo_shadow_probe.py`), whose shadow definitions were not compared here, or that the paired set `common` shifts the target classification in a way the code review above did not catch. Resolving it is a tool question and belongs to the tool lane. The OURS-side half of FINDING 3 (28 in shadow / 44 not, against v1's 29/75) moves with the roster and is expected to.
